As I said in the OP, I'm familiar with the argument that feminism is about equality. I'm also familiar with the general history of feminism.
All is well, I wasn't looking for one, always up for one thou but yeah the point I was trying to make is that a lot of people in general misconstrue the meaning of the word.

The word has several possible meanings and I agree a definition should be nailed down right at the start of any discussion. It can refer to the movement as a whole, (the people and organizations involved) an ideology, (the ideas that drive the goals of those people) One supposed particular goal only, (outcome equality between the sexes) multiple related goals, and I'm sure other things as well.

Tangentially related to the topic, language is dynamic. Words and languages evolve, occasionally radically. Not only in connotation, but denotation. Heated terms are particularly subject to this. Regardless of one definition or the other, most people without bias one way or the other would generally regard a feminist as a good thing - as somebody who simply supports equal rights for people regardless of gender. I'd certainly have identified as a feminist not long ago, but it has reached a point where I think feminism is becoming more equated with hate, prejudice, and ironic sexism than it is with rational equality. The reason is simple. A disproportionate number of the people who identify as being a feminist, at least as a major component of their identity, tend to be the sorts to focus much more on the former than the latter.
